# Copilot code review instructions

This repository wraps the Nat20 D&D 5e rules engine (`nat20_core`) in a typed JSON-lines API over stdio, for an AI-run game on the 2024 rules (SRD 5.2.1). `CLAUDE.md` holds the full project rules; this file says what a reviewer checks and how to report it. Where the two disagree, `CLAUDE.md` wins.

## How to review

- Pull requests here are routinely several hundred lines. That size is accepted. Review the whole diff, but never flag a PR for being large or ask for it to be split.
- Report a finding only when it changes behaviour, breaks a rule below, breaks the wire contract, leaks hidden data to a player, breaks a licence rule, or would turn CI red. Each finding must name the realistic input or path that triggers it.
- Use High for rule, contract, visibility, licence and SRD violations and for wrong game outcomes. Use Medium for other real defects: a crash, a flaky or wrong test, a fixture that no longer matches, a missing required update (CHANGELOG, generated files, TASKS.md row).
- Do not report Low or informational findings. No comments on style, formatting, naming, wording, comment text, doc phrasing, import order, or "consider" refactors. `cargo fmt`, `clippy -D warnings` and `tsc` already gate those in CI.
- Do not ask for human approval of choices that are already recorded. A decision in `docs/decisions/`, `contract/protocol.md`, a milestone spec in `docs/milestones/`, or the PR description's Before / After / How is settled; review the code against it, not the choice itself. Known gaps that have a `TASKS.md` row or a `not_implemented` answer are not findings.
- When nothing meets this bar, report no issues and recommend approval. Do not list minor observations to fill the review.
- Do not repeat a finding that a reply on its thread already answered with a reason, unless the new code still has the defect.

## Project rules to enforce

1. **Contract first.** Every wire type (command, field, event, error code, view type) lives only in `crates/nat20-api-contract/`. Flag wire types defined in the server or written by hand in TypeScript, `nat20_core` types in the contract or re-exported through the API, and logic, helpers or extra dependencies in the contract crate (it may depend on serde, serde_json and schemars only). Every contract type and field needs a doc comment. A change that crosses the engine boundary must, in the same PR, update a fixture in `contract/fixtures/`, add a `contract/CHANGELOG.md` line with the new version, and commit regenerated files. Flag any hand edit to `generated/` or `packages/engine-client/src/generated/`.
2. **Schema shapes the TS generator mishandles.** Tagged enums use struct variants, never newtype variants. No `#[schemars(required)]` on an `Option`. A new `#[serde(flatten)]` of a tagged enum needs its Rust name in the `flattened` map of `tools/codegen/gen.mjs`.
3. **Versioning.** `CONTRACT_VERSION` is `1.0.0-dev.N` until v1 ships, so breaking changes are allowed, but each needs its CHANGELOG line. Flag anything that weakens the `hello` schema-hash check or lets a client start on a mismatch.
4. **Visibility is structural.** Player-facing view types never carry HP, AC, DCs, roll targets (`against`), `dc_source`, monster stat blocks, scenario data or DM reasoning, not even in free-text `text` or `message` fields and not as optional "maybe hidden" fields. Players, the roller included, see dice, total and outcome only. Enemy health reaches players only as a band (`unhurt`, `bloodied`, `down`). `crates/nat20-api-server/src/projection.rs` is the only code that turns state into a view. A player agent's tools bind `viewer` to its own handle; flag any path where an agent picks its viewer. Every new field that describes a creature, roll, check or scenario needs its row in the visibility table in `contract/protocol.md`.
5. **The engine rolls.** Only the engine decides that a roll happens and resolves it. Flag any command, tool, agent or test helper that sets a roll result, check outcome, damage or HP directly. Roll ids (`rN`) are session-unique and never reused or rewritten. The DM agent picks checks from the scenario or the SRD DC ladder and never rules success.
6. **Core boundary.** Only `crates/nat20-api-server/src/adapter/` may `use nat20_core`. Flag code that works around a core rule instead of fixing it in the fork. `nat20_core` is pinned by `rev`; a rev bump belongs in its own PR. Flag a git dependency pinned by `branch` instead of `rev` or taken from a repo that isn't ours, a `[patch.crates-io]` entry in the workspace `Cargo.toml`, and a direct dependency on hecs, parry3d, uom or rerecast once core re-exports them (UPS-15). Flag a committed `.cargo/config.toml` that patches `nat20_core` to a local path.
7. **Content and licences.** No text from WotC books or D&D Beyond, and no Foundry dnd5e text, art, pregens or 2014 packs (Foundry structured fields from CC-BY-4.0 records only). No GPL, AGPL, LGPL-only or CC-BY-SA code or data; MPL-2.0 only in an unmodified third-party crate named as an exception in `deny.toml`. SRD content needs CC-BY-4.0 attribution.
8. **Tasks, PRs, CI.** `TASKS.md` is the only task list: flag new TODO comments with no matching row. Never skip, disable, ignore or quarantine a test to get green. A decision with real alternatives needs a record in `docs/decisions/` in the same PR; an accepted record is superseded by a new one, never rewritten. Fixture transcripts are seeded and must stay deterministic: flag tests that depend on an unseeded roll.
9. **Dependencies point down.** `nat20_core` depends on nothing of ours, nothing depends on `game/`, and no client talks to the engine except through the game loop.

## SRD 5.2.1 rules validation

The game must follow the 2024 rules as written in the System Reference Document 5.2.1 (CC-BY-4.0). The SRD text is not in this repository, so work from your knowledge of SRD 5.2.1.

- Check every change that touches a game mechanic against the SRD: d20 tests (attack rolls, ability checks, saving throws), Advantage and Disadvantage, critical hits, damage and damage types, Hit Points, Temporary Hit Points, healing, death saving throws, rests and Hit Point Dice, conditions, exhaustion, actions, bonus actions, reactions, movement, initiative and surprise, cover, spellcasting, monster stat blocks, scene checks, DCs and hazards. That covers `crates/nat20-api-server/src/adapter/`, `scene.rs`, `render.rs`, scenario and registry JSON, pregens, and the fixtures that record outcomes.
- When the code contradicts SRD 5.2.1, report a High finding that names the SRD section (for example "Playing the Game › D20 Tests › Attack Rolls" or "Rules Glossary › Exhaustion"), states what the SRD says, and states what the code does instead.
- The 2024 rules win. 2014 (SRD 5.1) data may fill a field the 2024 rules leave out, never override a 2024 rule. Flag 2014 behaviour that differs from 2024, such as 2014 exhaustion levels or the 2014 surprise rule.
- Example of the kind of bug to catch: treating a natural 20 or 1 as automatic success or failure on an ability check or saving throw. SRD 5.2.1 gives that effect only to attack rolls ("Attack Rolls › Rolling 20 or 1"), and death saving throws have their own natural 20 and 1 rule (a natural 20 regains 1 Hit Point).
- Known data bugs to flag if reintroduced: 5e-bits applies the Goblin Warrior's extra 1d4 damage on every hit, but the rule grants it only with Advantage; the SRD text scrambles the ability scores of Ancient Red Dragon, Remorhaz and Will-o'-Wisp, so those three take 5e-bits numbers.
- Do not flag things the demo deliberately leaves out: character creation, level-up, long rests, loot, vision and darkvision, Hide and Stealth, grappling, Weapon Mastery, Heroic Inspiration, magic items other than Potions of Healing, subclasses.
- If you are not sure what the SRD says, do not report a finding.
